claims.head: Heavyweight bout
claims.body: The Ducks are near the top of the league for shot volume, but the Devils are one of the best at keeping shots away. We’ll side with the Devils’ defense.
claims.call: The Devils keep the Ducks’ shot volume score under 100, the league average.
claims.see: Fewer than 46 shot attempts for the Ducks at 5-on-5, which usually means 28 or fewer shots on goal on the scoreboard.
claims.nums: Anaheim 8th for shot volume (score 106) · New Jersey 5th for keeping shots away

New Jersey: shots-against score 93, 5th of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 9 and 9 games this season.

claims.head: Like for like: Mantha against Killorn
claims.call: The Devils’ L3 (Mantha, Rodrigues and Mercer) spends at least 34% of its 5-on-5 time against the Ducks’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Devils keep sending Mantha’s line (Mantha, Rodrigues and Mercer) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Sheldon Keefe keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Ducks’ third line is Killorn, McQueen and Colangelo.
claims.nums: At home: 34% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against third lines, about 23% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Sheldon Keefe likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Ducks’ third line.
claims.cite: Matchups · New Jersey home games this season · 6 games, 47 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: New Jersey’s L3 (Mantha, Rodrigues and Mercer) at home: 34% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ third lines. Matchups, New Jersey home games this season, 6 games, 47 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face third lines about 23% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

check.measure: share of New Jersey L3's 5-on-5 time against Anaheim L3
check.rule: held if the share is at or above the home habit; partly if above the no-matching level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Nobody’s sitting back in this one
claims.call: The game’s pace score is above 106, faster than either team’s usual.
claims.see: More than 70 shots between them at 5-on-5, on goal or wide, which usually means 57 or more shots on goal on the scoreboard.
claims.body: The Ducks play some of the league’s fastest games, and so do the Devils. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
claims.nums: Pace score (100 is league average): Anaheim 3rd (106), New Jersey 7th (103)

claims.head: The Devils better keep their heads up
claims.body: On physicality, Anaheim is one of the league’s best, but New Jersey is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Ducks.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 9 games cover only 26% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 41%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Luke Evangelista returned in their last game after missing 3 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Connor Brown returned in their last game after missing 8 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Johnathan Kovacevic was added to the roster on Oct 11 and has played beside Declan Chisholm.

NJD.head: The Devils should be in control
NJD.body: New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Anaheim will be without Terry. The Ducks’ best way in is piling up shots.

ANA.head: The Ducks are up against it
ANA.body: New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Anaheim will be without Terry. To pull this off, the Ducks can start with piling up shots, plus a goalie who steals the show.

story.head: The Ducks are searching for answers
